# PLAN — iteration 2
## Current state assessment
Iteration 1 passed simulation and routed timing, but its inline 3-bit counter implementation measured the same 3 LUTs and 4 FFs as the timing-feasible incumbent, so it was rejected for no strict `minimize_luts` improvement. Timing recovery is not available as a promotion path because the incumbent already meets setup and hold.

## Hypothesis
A 4-bit Johnson sequence may reduce counter next-state logic enough to lower LUT use, at the cost of one additional FF; the routed utilization report will determine whether it improves the objective.

## Instruction for generator
In `debouncer_top`, replace the 3-bit binary count state with a 4-bit Johnson sequence that advances through `0000, 0001, 0011, 0111, 1111, 1110, 1100, 1000`; clear it synchronously when `noisy == clean`, and on the eighth differing sample (`count == 4'b1000`) update `clean` to `noisy` and clear the sequence. Preserve the synchronous active-high reset, registered `clean`, exact eight-sample behavior, and `// @latency 0`; do not add pipeline stages. Promote only if all fixed verification and routed metric gates pass and LUT use is strictly below the incumbent’s 3 LUTs.
